activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Inhomogeneous ODEs With Sinusoidal Forcing

examples.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d} x^2} + 4y = 4\sin 2x
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x) = A \cos{2x} + B \sin{2x} - x \cos{2x},
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d} x^2} + 4y = 4\sin 2x, \qquad y(0) = 2 , \ \ y'(0) = -3.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We find the constants $A$ and $B$ by substituting the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(0)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A\operatorname{cos}⁡0+B\operatorname{sin}⁡0-0\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\ 2 & =A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Differentiating $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-2A\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2B\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x) \\  & =-2A\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2B\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y'(0)=-3$ into the derivative gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & =-2A\operatorname{sin}⁡0+2B\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0+2(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0 \\ -3 & =2B-1 \\ -2 & =2B \\ -1 & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $A=2$ and $B=-1,$ we have the following solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+25y=-20\operatorname{cos}⁡5x-10\operatorname{sin}⁡5x
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A\operatorname{cos}⁡5x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡5x,$ find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
feedback.worked_solution:
The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form $\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x$ because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x)+5x(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡5x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =10(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡5x)-25x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x)\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
10(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡5x)-25x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x)+25x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡5x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡5x)=-20\operatorname{cos}⁡5x-10\operatorname{sin}⁡5x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
-10\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡5x+10\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡5x=-20\operatorname{cos}⁡5x-10\operatorname{sin}⁡5x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10\beta =-20\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡5x) \\ -10\alpha =-10\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡5x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =1$ and $\beta =-2.$ Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡5x-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡5x.
$$
